originalTitle: Manipal Health IPO: Co. garners Rs 4,167 crore from anchor investors; ADIA, Morgan Stanley among investors
simplifiedContent: Manipal Health Enterprises, a company that wants to list its shares on the stock market, has already collected a large amount of money, Rs 4,167 crore, from important investors before its initial public offering (IPO) even starts. The IPO is scheduled to begin on July 29 and the company hopes to raise a total of Rs 9,275 crore. As part of this IPO, the company will issue new shares and some existing shareholders will sell their shares. The money raised will be used to pay off debts and buy other hospitals to expand its network. This is significant because it shows that big investors like ADIA and Morgan Stanley are interested in the company, which could attract more investors when the IPO opens.

originalTitle: Boeing shares rise 5% despite higher than expected Q2 loss on Air Force One costs
simplifiedContent: Boeing, a big airplane maker, recently reported that it lost more money than expected in the second quarter of the year. This loss was partly due to a $280 million charge related to the company's work on the Air Force One planes. Despite this loss, Boeing's stock price went up 5%, which means investors are feeling more positive about the company. This is because Boeing also reported some good news, including making more cash and producing more planes, which suggests that the company is making progress in its efforts to get back on track. This progress is a positive sign for investors, which is why the company's stock price rose despite the reported loss.

originalTitle: Fusion Finance forfeits unpaid rights shares after final reminder
simplifiedContent: Fusion Finance had some investors who didn't pay the full amount for their shares, even after being reminded. As a result, the company took away 1.63 lakh shares that weren't fully paid for, which were worth Rs 1.07 crore. On the other hand, some investors did pay the remaining amount, and the company turned 2.29 lakh shares into fully paid shares after receiving Rs 1.50 crore from them. This means that Fusion Finance now has fewer partly paid shares and more fully paid shares. This matters because it can affect the company's finances and the value of its shares.

originalTitle: Treasury yields retreat as oil tumbles before Fed policy decision
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the interest rates on US government bonds, called Treasury yields, have gone down. This happened at the same time that oil prices dropped. The change in Treasury yields is important because it's happening just before the Federal Reserve (or "Fed") makes a decision about monetary policy. This decision could affect the overall direction of the economy and the stock market. The drop in Treasury yields might be a sign that investors are waiting to see what the Fed will decide before making any big moves.

originalTitle: Crude prices extend decline, fall over 5% on US-Iran talks optimism; Brent down 20% in three sessions
simplifiedContent: The price of crude oil, which is the raw material used to make gasoline and other fuels, has fallen by over 5% due to hopes of improved relations between the US and Iran. This is because people think that if the US and Iran can come to an agreement, there will be less chance of disruptions to oil supplies. As a result, the price of Brent crude oil has dropped to $80.67 and US crude oil (WTI) has dropped to $77.83. This is a big drop, with Brent crude oil down by 20% in just three days. This matters because it can affect the cost of gasoline and other fuels, as well as the performance of companies that deal with oil.

originalTitle: Pentagon blacklist of CXMT: Is Washington accidentally creating a stronger Chinese chip rival?
simplifiedContent: A Chinese company called CXMT just started selling its shares on the Shanghai Stock Exchange and had a very successful first day, with its value increasing by 466%. This means the company is now worth a lot of money, 3.28 trillion yuan. The US has put CXMT on a "blacklist" which creates problems for the company, but it also motivates CXMT to focus on making its own computer chips in China. This could affect the global market for a type of computer memory called DRAM. The US actions may have an unintended consequence of making CXMT a stronger competitor in the long run.
